summary: After June's sharp pullback — chips down ~10%, nuclear giving back 30%, quantum cut nearly in half — Brian argues Micron's blowout quarter (revenue up 346%, ~85% gross margins, AI memory sold out through 2026 with shortages into 2028) proves the AI buildout is accelerating, not cooling, and the dip created entries across eight names. His core: Eaton (ETN, BUY) with ~$3.4M of electrical content per megawatt of AI compute and data-center orders up 240%; BWX Technologies (BWXT, BUY), the only profitable nuclear name and sole builder of US Navy reactors, carrying a record $8.6B backlog; Nvidia (NVDA, BUY), the CUDA-software monopoly whose revenue grew 8x in three years while its PE fell from over 100 to ~30, PEG ~0.5, bought on its 200-day line; Broadcom (AVGO, BUY), the anti-Nvidia custom-chip play with AI revenue nearly tripling and a $73B order book, PEG ~0.5; and Alphabet (GOOGL, BUY), the cheapest mega at ~24x forward earnings with Cloud growing 63% and ~$460B of signed future work. Conditional on further pullbacks: Arista (ANET, CONDITIONAL_BUY) at 44x forward earnings — he wants it near its 50-day line — and Rambus (RMBS, CONDITIONAL_BUY), the memory-interface shovel seller, kept small at ~60x earnings while it answers a DOJ document request. Fabrinet (FN, BUY) is the pure-play optical factory whose constraint is capacity, not orders. His portfolio construction: heavy on mega caps scaling down to small caps — asymmetric by design. A Seeking Alpha sponsorship segment is included.
title: Dips Don't Last – 8 Stocks I'm Buying
